name: Andrew Horton
why_notable: New Zealand security researcher who created WhatWeb and still maintains it. He released version 0.3 at Kiwicon III in Wellington on 2 November 2009, as part of a talk on scanning all of New Zealand's web space. At the same presentation he published bing-ip2hosts, gggooglescan and basedomainname for finding targets, and he also released geoipgen, which used a GeoIP database in reverse to turn a country into a list of IP ranges. WhatWeb's plugin architecture, with passive and aggressive matches, aggression levels and logging formats built for large datasets, made it a standard web-fingerprinting tool in Kali and in pentest curricula. He revived the project in 2025-2026 with the 0.6.x releases.
